newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices recover with heat, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices recover with heat, NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices continued their seesaw pattern Thursday, as a recovering futures market and warmer forecasts across the East and Midwest swung prices higher, traders said.
At 1334 EDT, NYMEX's September contract had risen to a high of $2.55, up 7.8 cents from Wednesday's settlement.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices at the Henry Hub returned to Tuesday's levels in the low-to-mid $2.50s, regaining 12 cents from Wednesday.
In the Midwest, swing prices jumped 10 cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
At the Chicago city-gate, where temperatures are forecast to climb to highs in the mid-80s F by Saturday, prices were also quoted sharply higher in the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s.

Strength in the Gulf and an unexpected outage also prompted more buying in the West Texas market. Permian Basin prices regained eight cents to the mid-$2.40s, while Waha was lifted again into the high-$2.40s to about $2.50.

El Paso was cutting 225 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas in the San Juan Basin today for unscheduled repairs at its Gallup C gas processing plant in New Mexico. The plant, which was shut this morning due to a leak, is expected to return to service Friday.
Normal capacity at the plant is about 2.85 billion cubic feet per day.

Scheduled maintenance is also underway at El Paso's Keystone Mainline Station in Texas, where about 400 mmcfd has been affected at receipt points in the Permian Basin since Tuesday. The outage, which is set to end today, has also impacted about 185 mmcfd of supply at Waha.
Southern California border prices similarly recovered eight cents to the low-$2.50s.

In the East, prices at the New York city gate swung between $2.68 and $2.78, indicating a gain of about 10 cents from Wednesday's depressed levels. A high of 87 degrees F is expected to arrive in New York Saturday, according to Weather Services Corp.
